text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition can't explain this outcome: you and the successful candidate are both men, so sex can't distinguish between you. An all-male panel is worth noting as a general governance weakness, but as an argument in *your* case it's a non-starter — and raising it will make your complaint look unfocused.

Your real argument is strong without it: on the published criteria you appear better qualified for leadership (master's in educational leadership, five years as deputy) than someone with "courses in school leadership." That's a merit-based challenge.

Act on the silence instead. Send a written follow-up citing your right to reasons, note any deadline for appeal, and ask for the scoring criteria and how each finalist was rated.
